name: TRE
workload: Find all matches of 15 regex patterns over a ~20 MB English e-book (mtent12.txt), best of 5 runs per engine, wall time in ms, compiled with default engine options.
claimed_speedup: Mixed, not a project claim: on x86-64 Intel Xeon 2.67GHz TRE 0.8.0 beats PCRE2 10.10 on [a-zA-Z]+ing (954 ms vs 1373 ms, 1.44x, derived from page data) and .{0,2}(Tom|Sawyer|Huckleberry|Finn) (3425 ms vs 5164 ms, 1.51x, derived from page data), ties on .{2,4}(Tom|Sawyer|Huckleberry|Finn) (5248 ms vs 5298 ms). 32-bit Xeon run: 892 ms vs 1740 ms (1.95x derived), 3641 ms vs 6726 ms (1.85x derived), 5700 ms vs 7107 ms (1.25x derived). TRE is slower than PCRE2 on the other 12 of 15 patterns (e.g. Twain 486 ms vs 5 ms).
compiler_and_flags: GCC 4.8.2 (Linux) / GCC 4.4.7 (Windows run), engines and harness built with -g -O3 -Wall; TRE called via tre_regcomp(REG_EXTENDED|REG_NEWLINE) and tre_regnexec, PCRE2 via pcre2_compile(PCRE2_MULTILINE)/pcre2_match
hardware: Intel Xeon 2.67GHz (Linux, 64-bit and 32-bit runs); Intel Core i5 3.2GHz (Windows); exact CPU SKU not stated
tradeoffs: POSIX leftmost-longest matching with correct submatches, approximate (agrep-style) matching, wide-char and binary-safe APIs, thread safe, regexec does not allocate from the heap (README). No Perl-style backtracking semantics, so results can differ from PCRE2 on alternation; backreferences are exponential.
caveats: The evidence is a third-party comparison page by the author of the PCRE2 sljit JIT (Zoltan Herczeg, page last modified 2015-08-23), not a TRE claim. TRE loses on 12 of 15 patterns against plain PCRE2, and by 10x to 150x against PCRE2-JIT, Oniguruma and RE2 on many patterns; its two wins are on [a-zA-Z]+ing and the .{0,2}(alternation) pattern, and .{2,4}(alternation) is a 1 percent tie (a loss in the Windows run). Versions are TRE 0.8.0 and PCRE2 10.10 from 2015; current TRE and PCRE2 were not measured. Engines were not tuned (default options). PCRE2 uses leftmost-first Perl semantics and TRE leftmost-longest POSIX semantics, so match counts may differ. Benchmark harness is public as regex-test.tgz on the same gh-pages branch (read in this session: main.c, tre.c, pcre2.c, Makefile, MakeGlobals); tier A except the CPU is given only as 'Intel Xeon 2.67GHz'. Heng Li's regex benchmark (lh3lh3.users.sourceforge.net/reb.shtml) reportedly shows TRE third on alternation patterns but could not be opened here (redirect to a profile page), so it is not used.
found_via: seed-record pass: https://github.com/laurikari/tre/ (listed in awesome-cpp and awesome-c, Regex section); numbers found at the sljit regex_perf.html comparison page via WebSearch
